audit.whatIsWrong: 'His Steel Tempest (Q) out-ranges your Null Sphere' in early, repeated in whys[0].
audit.why: Steel Tempest is 475 range. Null Sphere is 650. You out-range his basic Q by 175 units, which is the opposite of what the page says and it is the one thing that makes the pre-6 lane survivable — you can clip the wave and chip him from outside his thrust. What actually beats you early is not his range but his economy: Steel Tempest is free and on a flat 4 seconds while Null Sphere costs 60 mana on 9 seconds at rank 1. Fixing the reason without fixing the conclusion would leave the reader standing too far back and starving.
audit.corrected: Steel Tempest is 475 range and Null Sphere is 650 — you reach him first. His edge is that his Q is free every 4 seconds while yours costs mana on 9.

audit.whatIsWrong: Wind Wall is named as the clock of the matchup in six strings. Its duration and cooldown are never given, and the page never says WHICH of your abilities it actually stops.
audit.why: Wind Wall is 25/23/21/19/17 seconds, 400 range, and it 'blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds'. Kassadin's kit carries exactly one projectile — Null Sphere — and the kit file says so explicitly ('can be blocked by Wind Wall-class effects'). Force Pulse is a cone with no projectile flag, Nether Blade is an empowered basic attack, and Riftwalk is a blink. So the wall turns off one quarter of your kit for four seconds, and the correct play is to lead with Force Pulse through it rather than to stand and wait, which is what 'hold your poke until it is spent' currently teaches. Twenty-five seconds at rank 1 against a four-second duration is also a very favourable ratio worth stating.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall stands 4 seconds on a 25s cooldown at rank 1. It eats Null Sphere; Force Pulse is a cone and goes straight through, as do your Nether Blade autos and Riftwalk.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yasuo.json (W description, cooldown 25/23/21/19/17, range 400, blocksProjectiles flag)

audit.whatIsWrong: 'blink in to punish him the instant his E is on cooldown' (mid) and 'blink in to punish his E cooldown' (whys[3]) — a window built on a cooldown that is effectively zero.
audit.why: Sweeping Blade is 0.5/0.4/0.3/0.2/0.1 seconds. It is never meaningfully down, so waiting for it is waiting forever. What Riot's text actually gates is the target: 'Cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds.' His mobility is therefore a function of how many units are standing near him, not of a cooldown bar. That flips the wave-management instruction on this page — a thin or crashed wave strands him, a big wave makes him untouchable, and neither is currently said.
audit.corrected: Sweeping Blade is half a second at rank 1 and never worth waiting out. What strands him is a dead wave, because he cannot re-dash the same unit for a few seconds.

audit.whatIsWrong: Last Breath is named as the payoff of his combo three times with no cooldown and no cast condition.
audit.why: It is 70/50/30 seconds at 1400 range and Riot's text is 'Blinks to an Airborne enemy champion'. It requires an airborne target, which is why the two-stack Steel Tempest whirlwind is the thing to dodge — deny the knockup and the ultimate has nothing to blink to. Seventy seconds at rank 1 is also a much more useful commit gate than Wind Wall's 25, since Wind Wall costs you a spell and Last Breath costs you the fight.
audit.corrected: Last Breath: 70s at rank 1, 1400 range, and it can only blink to an AIRBORNE champion. Dodge the whirlwind knockup and his ultimate has no entry.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yasuo.json (R description, cooldown 70/50/30, range 1400; Q knockup at 2 stacks)

audit.why: Sides and ratings left alone. Yasuo owning 1-5, Skill at 6 and the item stages back to him matches a free-cost champion with near-zero dash cooldowns against a mana-gated melee mage, and 53.85% over 52 games is the second-largest sample in my slice without being directional enough to move a cell.

Null Sphere interrupts channels and grants a magic-absorbing shield; it has never silenced in this kit version. Against Yasuo it is also the one spell Wind Wall deletes, which makes the fantasy of a lockout doubly misleading.
audit.corrected: Null Sphere interrupts channels; it does not silence.

audit.why: 53.85% over 52 games. The page quotes no figure. No change.

edits.before: Neither of you blows the other up at level 1, but Yasuo is the early aggressor here. His Steel Tempest (Q) out-ranges your Null Sphere, and once he can E through the wave he chips you while your Q is mana-hungry and on a long cooldown, so don't trade orbs you can't afford. His Windwall (W) eats your Null Sphere outright, so never throw it into a raised W; wait it out. Farm with Nether Blade autos to bank mana, concede the poke, and just reach 6 healthy.
edits.after: Neither of you blows the other up at level 1, but Yasuo is the early aggressor. Steel Tempest is 475 range against your 650, so you reach him first — what beats you is that his Q is free every 4 seconds while yours costs mana on 9. Wind Wall stands 4 seconds and eats Null Sphere outright, but Force Pulse is a cone and walks straight through it. Farm with Nether Blade autos to bank mana, concede the poke, and reach 6 healthy.

edits.after: Yasuo is the level-1 aggressor: Steel Tempest is free every 4s while Null Sphere costs mana on 9, and Wind Wall eats the orb outright.

edits.before: This is your weather-it window turning into your spike. Through 4-5 keep farming under tower, Nether Blade restoring your mana and maxed Q letting you eat his E-dash trades without dying to one combo. At 6, Riftwalk changes everything: when he E's in to stack the third-Q knockup that sets up Last Breath (R), blink away before the knockup lands, or blink in to punish him the instant his E is on cooldown. Bait the Windwall, then commit on his downtime.
edits.after: This is your weather-it window turning into your spike. Through 4-5 keep farming under tower, Nether Blade restoring your mana and a maxed Q letting you eat his dash trades without dying to one combo. At 6, Riftwalk changes everything: when he dashes in to land the whirlwind knockup that sets up Last Breath (70s at rank 1), blink out before it connects. Sweeping Blade is half a second, so stop waiting on it — what strands him is a dead wave he cannot re-dash.

notes: The Wind Wall interaction here is the exact class of gap flagged in the brief's calibration note about Azir. The page knew Wind Wall blocks Null Sphere but never said Force Pulse goes through it, which is the difference between having a level-6 combo and not having one. Worth a repo-wide check: every Kassadin page that mentions a projectile-blocking wall should say which of Q/W/E/R it actually stops, and the kit file already answers that (kitFlags.projectile lists Q only). Two smaller things I left alone: the page spells it 'Windwall' in four content strings where Riot's name is 'Wind Wall' (I normalised only inside strings I was already rewriting), and Steel Tempest's two-stack whirlwind does travel further than the listed 475, but the kit file publishes only the one range so I stated 475 for the base thrust and did not put a number on the tornado.
